newsitem.title: IRAQ: Russia wants to fly goods to Iraq under oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants to fly goods to Iraq under oil deal.

text.p: An Iraqi government newspaper said on Sunday that a Russian airlines was seeking permission to fly food and medicine to Iraq under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.

Al-Jumhouriya newspaper quoted the director-general of state-run Iraqi Airways, Rabee' Mohammed Saleh, as saying that the Russian airlines had informed him that it had submitted the request to the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq.

"The Russian airlines sent a telegram to Iraqi Airways informing it that it had submitted a request to the U.N. sanctions committee to allow it to transport foodstuffs and medicine to Iraq and it is waiting for approval," the paper said.
It said several other European and Arab airlines had also asked for permission from the United Nations to do the same thing.

"Several international airlines have submitted similar requests to transport food and medicine and take with them sick Iraqis. They are German, French, Dutch, African, British and Jordanian companies," it added.
Iraq is under stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The sanctions -- which bar Baghdad from exporting its oil -- have prevented flights to and from Iraq.

Baghdad started limited oil sales under an oil agreement signed with the United Nations in December. Under the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis.
A number of Iraqi civil airliners are grounded in Amman, Tunis and possibly other foreign cities to which they were sent before Iraq came under attack during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
The U.N. committee has so far refused to allow the planes to fly back to Iraq on grounds they are an economic resource whose return would be a breach of sanctions.
